entities.summary: Lê Hy Tông was the 21st emperor of the Vietnamese Later Lê dynasty, reigning from 1698 to 1716. Born in 1663 in Hanoi, he succeeded his half-brother and predecessor, Emperor Cảnh Tông, and initially faced significant challenges from the Tây Sơn rebels. Despite these challenges, Lê Hy Tông implemented various reforms, including the reorganization of the imperial examination system and the promotion of Buddhism. His reign is often characterized as a period of relative stability and cultural revival in Vietnam. The legacy of Lê Hy Tông can be seen in the many cultural and architectural achievements of the Later Lê dynasty, including the construction of the Thăng Long Citadel and the development of Vietnamese art and literature. As a result of his efforts, the Later Lê dynasty continued to thrive until its eventual collapse in the 19th century. Despite the passage of time, Lê Hy Tông remains an important figure in Vietnamese history, remembered for his dedication to the welfare of his people and his role in shaping the country's cultural identity.
